source: reconstruction of the release cache poisoning write-ups (2024), on GitLab
note: The cache poisoning shape of the 2024 write-ups, reproduced on GitLab (the published cases are GitHub runs that cannot be replayed offline): one cache under default:, keyed on a constant, so the merge request lint job saves the store the tag-triggered publish job restores, with the project's separate caches for protected branches turned off. The lint job installs pnpm by piping a fetched script into sh, so whoever controls that script writes into the cache. Walked one hop along the cache edge, the path reaches the publish job, which holds NPM_TOKEN (a tag pipeline receives protected variables) and runs npm publish: Critical. Neither job declares the cache itself, so the edge exists only through default: inheritance.
